os_read.pledge: NET REVENUES = Net Water System Revenues + Net Hydroelectric System Revenues (Revenues of each system minus its O&M). The retail Energy System (electric distribution, ~8,000 customers, $80.0M of 2005/2012/2013 obligations) is SEPARATE and its revenues are NOT pledged and NOT available for these bonds. Hydro-vs-water split: FY2014 actual revenue was almost entirely Water System (water sales $12.0M + transfers $3.9M + 1% property tax $2.9M); hydro contributed little (cost-reimbursement only) because the PG&E power contract had expired. Projections (FY15-19) assume merchant hydro energy sales of $6.3-8.8M vs water sales $17-22M, i.e. ~25-30% of pro-forma revenue is HYDRO and is merchant-priced + hydrology-dependent. OS expressly warns: 'Lower electric rates and reduction in water flow through the Hydroelectric System could result in materially lower Hydroelectric System revenues.' Water side is a strong agricultural irrigation district: pre-1914 Merced River water rights, 605,000 AF storage licenses, ~164,000 irrigated acres, pop ~140,000, 2,200+ customers, $3.15M annual standby-charge revenue.
os_read.lien: Senior/first lien on Net Revenues. After this 2014 refunding NO parity obligations remain outstanding. The 2005 Bonds/2005 Installment Payments are pledged Net Hydroelectric Revenues SUBORDINATE to the 2014 Bonds. (Note: only the small $725k taxable 2014B series is junior to certain Energy obligations on hydro net revenues; OUR bond is the tax-exempt 2014A and has the clean senior claim.)
os_read.rate_covenant: Net Revenues (Net Water + Net Hydro combined) >= 125% of Debt Service each Fiscal Year, with the proviso that Rate-Stabilization-Fund transfers IN to revenues are capped at 25% of debt service for covenant purposes. Historic Water-System-only coverage on the small 2008 debt was 3.22x (FY2014)/1.78x (FY2013). Projected combined coverage on the larger 2014 debt (~$2.74M/yr) is 3.0-3.3x but that leans on the merchant-hydro revenue materializing.
os_read.dsrf: SURETY. Reserve Fund Requirement $2,405,740.25 satisfied by an AGM (Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp.) municipal-bond debt-service-reserve insurance policy, not cash. Separately a Rate Stabilization Fund seeded ~$1,500,000 cash at closing.
os_read.abt: Additional parity bonds permitted (Additional Indebtedness caption) subject to a Net-Revenues coverage test; District covenants no parity senior to 2014 Bonds beyond the indenture's ABT. Subordinate hydro pledges (2005 obligations) and an unsecured $25M Wells Fargo line are carved out as junior/unsecured.
os_read.insurance: Insured by Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (AGM). Underlying rating not separately printed on the EMMA security page (shows S&P insured rating). DSRF also AGM surety.
os_read.oid: Yes - modest original issue discount (offered at 97.873, i.e. ~2.13 pts below par). De-minimis-relevant but shallow at issue; current deep secondary discount is a rate-driven mark, not an OID matter.

orders.dd_basis: WCFFA Wastewater (Green) essential-service REVENUE/UTILITY, tax-exempt, TEY exact — BUT tape STALE 57d (>30d) & thin (12 prints/yr), and JPA financing-authority/installment structure caveat | OS READ CONFIRM (strongest of 4): FIRST lien Net Revenues, 120% covenant, UNINSURED but AA-/Aa3 underlying, 91% flat-charge revenue, Teeter. CAVEAT: NO DSRF, ~$35M parity SRF loans, coverage leans on adopted rate increases (FY21 audited would have been sub-1.0x)

os_read.pledge: INSTALLMENT-SALE / Marks-Roos JPA. West County Facilities Financing Authority (a JPA of West County Wastewater District + CSCDA, formed 8/1/2021) issues; bonds payable from Installment Payments made by WEST COUNTY WASTEWATER DISTRICT under an Installment Purchase Agreement (9/1/2021). The Installment Payments are a special obligation of the District, secured by a pledge of and FIRST LIEN on ALL NET REVENUES of the District's wastewater Enterprise (Gross Revenues - O&M). Gross Revenues are broad: all sewer charges PLUS the District's share of County property-tax/tax-increment (redevelopment) allocation PLUS investment earnings; EXCLUDES connection fees and ad-valorem taxes levied to pay GO bonds. Underlying agency = West County Wastewater District (sanitary district founded 1921; western Contra Costa County - San Pablo, parts of Pinole and Richmond, Tara Hills, North Richmond, El Sobrante, etc.; 16.9 sq mi, ~34,000 residences + ~900 commercial, pop ~104,000). DIVERSIFIED ratepayer base: top-10 customers only 11.2% of charges, largest (EBMUD) 4.4%. ~91% of sewer revenue is FLAT charges (consumption-independent, drought-resilient). Billed on the County property-tax roll under a TEETER PLAN -> District receives 100% of billed amounts, no delinquency exposure.
os_read.lien: FIRST LIEN on Net Revenues, SHARED on a PARITY with four 2015 SWRCB State Revolving Fund (SRF) Loans (~$35.1M total outstanding at 1.0-1.9%). The District covenants it will NOT issue any obligation SENIOR to the Installment Payments (no senior debt permitted). Subordinate debt is permitted under a separate 100% MADS test.
os_read.rate_covenant: Net Revenues (Gross + Rate-Stabilization-Fund transfers - O&M) >= 120% of Installment Payments + parity DS each Fiscal Year, layered on a sum-sufficient cascade (pay O&M first, then IPs+parity, then other indenture amounts, then additional payments). PRO-FORMA coverage (Table 12) is strong: historical 7.65x/6.90x/4.09x on the small SRF-only DS, settling to ~2.25x/2.49x/2.29x then ~1.64x/1.73x/1.76x (FY24-26) once the 2021 Revenue Bonds (~$4.78M/yr DS) layer on top - comfortably above the 120% covenant. CAVEAT: FY2020-21 AUDITED net revenues dipped to $4.85M (elevated O&M + a depressed year); against post-bond total DS ~$7.49M that single year would have been ~0.65x. The projected 1.6-1.8x recovery DEPENDS on the adopted 5.5%/yr (then 3%) rate increases being realized - rate execution is the key variable.
os_read.dsrf: NONE. This deal has NO debt-service reserve fund - the TOC and Security section carry only a Rate Stabilization Fund (held by the District, NOT pledged to the bonds), no Reserve Fund/surety. Unusual vs the older insured deals; consistent with a strong-underlying-rating uninsured structure.
os_read.abt: 120% MADS test. New parity obligations require: no default; AND Net Revenues for the most recent 12 months (ending <=60 days before adoption) >= 120% of Maximum Annual Debt Service on the Installment Payments + all parity to be outstanding (Additional Revenues may be added). Refunding parity that lowers aggregate DS is exempt from (a)/(b). Subordinate obligations allowed on a 100% MADS test.
os_read.insurance: NONE (uninsured). UNDERLYING ratings are strong on their own: S&P AA- and Moody's Aa3 assigned directly to the bonds. Kestrel Verifiers 'Green Bond' second-party opinion (ICMA Green Bond Principles) - a use-of-proceeds label, NOT a credit enhancement.
os_read.issue_price: 120.624% / 1.68% yield (initial offering field on EMMA for this 4% 06/01/2041 maturity). The overall issue ($79,575,000) was sold at a large net original-issue PREMIUM ($16,157,183 premium; UW purchase price $95,602,095.50 = par - $130,088 discount + $16.16M premium). Underwriter Piper Sandler & Co.
os_read.oid: No - this is a PREMIUM bond (120.6% at issue). De-minimis-favorable (premium amortizes, no ordinary-income accretion). Current deep secondary discount is a rate-driven mark, not OID.
